'''Antígona Segura Peralta''' (born September 20, 1971) is a Mexican physicist and [[Astrobiology|astrobiologist]]. Since 2006, she has been a researcher at the Institute of Nuclear Sciences of the [[National Autonomous University of Mexico]] (UNAM) and collaborator at the [[NASA Astrobiology Institute]].<ref name=NAI>{{Cite web |url=https://astrobiology.nasa.gov/nai/directory/segura-peralta-antigona/ |title=Antigona Segura-Peralta |publisher=[[NASA Astrobiology Institute]] |access-date=2022-01-18}}</ref> As a [[Feminism|feminist]] she actively advocates for the inclusion of women in the [[exact sciences]], mathematics, and engineering.<ref name=busca>{{Cite web |url=https://distintaslatitudes.net/historias/serie/cientificas/antigona-segura-astrobiologa-mexicana |title=Antígona Segura, la astrobióloga mexicana que busca vida en otros mundos |trans-title=Antígona Segura, the Mexican Astrobiologist Who Searches for Life on Other Worlds |first=Ketzalli |last=Rosas |work=Distintas Latitudes |language=Spanish |date=August 20, 2018 |access-date=2022-01-18}}</ref> Segura has participated in several activities in and outside UNAM defending women's rights; she was awarded with the 2021 Hermila Galindo medal by the [[Congress of Mexico City]].<ref name=":0" />

==Academic training==
Antígona Segura graduated with a degree in [[Theoretical physics|Theoretical Physics]] from the [[Universidad Autónoma de San Luis Potosí|Autonomous University of San Luis Potosí]]. There she met the astronomer Miguel Ángel Herrera, with whom she conducted scientific research in a project directed by [[Arcadio Poveda]]. In 1997, she completed a master's degree in Astronomy at the {{ill|Institute of Astronomy of the National Autonomous University of Mexico|es|Instituto de Astronomía de la Universidad Nacional Autónoma de México|lt=UNAM Institute of Astronomy}}, and the same year she obtained a diploma in [[Science communication|Science Communication]] from UNAM's General Directorate for Scientific Outreach.<ref name=sigiDirectorio>{{Cite web |url=https://sigi.nucleares.unam.mx/sgiicn/people/user/view/id/63 |title=Directorio Académico |publisher=[[National Autonomous University of Mexico]] |language=Spanish |access-date=2022-01-18}}</ref>

She earned her doctorate in the Earth Sciences postgraduate program at UNAM with the thesis ''Fijación de nitrógeno por relámpagos volcánicos en el Marte primitivo'' (Nitrogen Fixation by Volcanic Lightning on Primitive Mars), advised by {{ill|Rafael Navarro González|es}}. From 2005 to 2006, she worked as a postdoctoral researcher at the [[Jet Propulsion Laboratory]] (JPL) associated with the [[California Institute of Technology]] (Caltech).<ref name=NAI/>

==Career and research==
Segura's research is focused on the study of planetary atmospheres and the remote detection of signs of life. She also collaborates on a multidisciplinary project on the formation and conditions of the early solar system.<ref name=sigiDirectorio/> She has determined possible sources of energy for the generation of [[Nitrogen fixation|fixed nitrogen]] on [[Atmosphere of Mars#Early atmosphere|primitive Mars]], proposing [[volcanic lightning]] as a new source.<!-- See "Nitrogen fixation on early Mars by volcanic lightning and other sources" under Publications -->

Her studies on [[biosignature]]s on habitable planets around [[Red dwarf|M dwarf]] stars reopened the debate about the habitability of planets that revolve around these types of stars, and have been used to argue in favor of astronomical observation programs to better understand the processes that generate the [[Chromosphere|chromospheric activity]] of the M dwarfs. Some examples are: Habitable Zones and M Dwarf Activity Across Time (HAZMAT),<ref>{{Cite journal |title=HAZMAT. II. Her research work has been developed at various institutions, such as the UNAM Institute of Nuclear Sciences,<ref>{{Cite web |url=https://www.fciencias.unam.mx/directorio/61397 |title=Dra. Antígona Segura Peralta |publisher=[[National Autonomous University of Mexico]] |language=Spanish |access-date=2022-01-18}}</ref> the NASA Jet Propulsion Laboratory,<ref name=NAI/> [[Pennsylvania State University]], and the UNAM Institute of Astronomy. In addition, she is a [[science communicator]], has worked at the news agency of the [[Mexican Academy of Sciences]], has written for the UNAM magazine ''{{ill|¿Cómo ves? (magazine)|es|¿Cómo ves? (revista)|lt=¿Cómo ves?}}'', and hosted the weekly radio program ''Hacia el Nuevo Milenio'' (Towards the New Millennium) on Radio Red AM.<ref name=busca/> She frequently gives talks to diverse audiences about astrobiology.

Antígona Segura was hired by the UNAM Institute of Nuclear Sciences in 2006.<ref name="busca" /> Currently, she is the only female researcher working in the Plasma Physics and Interaction of Radiation with Matter Department.<ref name=":0" />

==Activism==
Along with her scientific research, Segura has worked for women's human rights. She has focused on academic spaces that have been masculinized, like the Institute of Nuclear Sciences. In 2016, Segura was the only female candidate competing for the direction of the Institute of Nuclear Sciences,<ref>{{Cite journal |date=2016-08-23 |title=Prueban terna para dirigir el Instituto de Ciencias Nucleares |url=http://acervo.gaceta.unam.mx/index.php/gum10/article/view/81970 |journal=Gaceta UNAM (2010-2019) |language=es |issue=4790 |pages=1–18–19 }}</ref> and was the only candidate that proposed actions against gender inequality.<ref name=":1">{{Cite web |title=Antígona, la científica sancionada por la UNAM que será reconocida por el Congreso de la CDMX |url=https://www.proceso.com.mx/nacional/2022/3/23/antigona-la-cientifica-sancionada-por-la-unam-que-sera-reconocida-por-el-congreso-de-la-cdmx-282994.html |access-date=2022-03-28 |website=www.proceso.com.mx |language=spanish}}</ref>

Antígona Segura was sanctioned by the National Autonomous University of Mexico in 2018, after she advocated for a female student who was the victim of a sexual assault by a fellow student.<ref name=":1" />

In 2022, Antígona Segura was awarded with the Hermila Galindo Medal "for promoting women's equal access to the labor force."<ref name=":0" /> Two hundred people signed a petition requesting that her advocacy for women's rights be recognized.<ref name=":1" />
